quiz_title: 🧊 البرمجة ثلاثية الأبعاد للصغار - PicToBlox 3D - Challenge 5

questions.question: In our 3D First-Person Duck Hunter, what does first-person perspective mean?
options: Viewing the character from high above
Viewing the game world directly through the player's own virtual eyes
questions.explanation: Correct! First-person view locks the camera to the player's coordinate eyes, aiming outward.

questions.question: Which 3D coordinate represents the projectile trajectory vector to fire a bullet straight forward in depth?
options: Adding force along horizontal X axis
Adding velocity along depth Z axis
questions.explanation: Excellent! Pushing bullets along the depth Z axis shoots them forward into the virtual horizon.

questions.question: Which mouse event trigger is used to spawn and fire a bullet in our 3D shooter?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Clicking the mouse (or tapping screen) triggers the shooting script, launching projectile clones.

questions.question: What 3D shape is ideal for a bullet projectile in a duck hunting game?
questions.explanation: Spot on! Spheres represent bullet balls perfectly in 3D physics.

questions.question: What block is used to spawn a clone of a bullet at the player's camera position?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Cloning is the core mechanic to spawn individual flying bullets on every mouse click.

questions.question: How do you make the camera look around in 3D space when the player moves the mouse?
options: Map mouse movement coordinates (X, Y) to camera rotations
questions.explanation: Spot on! Tracking mouse motion and pivoting camera angle accordingly lets players look around the 3D world interactively!

questions.question: What event block triggers scripts in other sprites immediately when a target duck is hit by a bullet?
questions.explanation: Great! Broadcasting sends a signal across all running scripts, alerting sprites of the hit event.

questions.question: When a target duck sprite receives a 'hit' broadcast signal, what action should it perform to animate death?
options: Trigger physics gravity or downward Y velocity to make it fall down and disappear
questions.explanation: Perfect! Pulling the dead duck down along the Y-axis simulates gravitational falling realisticly.

questions.question: How can you check if a bullet has collided with or touched a flying duck in 3D space?
options: Using collision sensing or touching sprite blocks
questions.explanation: Spot on! 'touching (sprite)' or physics collision events identify impacts.

questions.question: Where should a bullet be spawned initially when the player clicks to fire?
options: At the exact current coordinate position of the Player Camera
questions.explanation: Perfect! Spawning the bullet at the camera coordinate makes it emerge directly from the player's weapon viewpoint.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to spawn a clone of 'Bullet' at the Camera's current coordinates when the mouse is down (clicked).
questions.task_hint: when mouse down? -> create clone of 'Bullet' -> set 3D position of clone to camera position
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Placing spawned bullet clones at the camera position is the core rule of first-person shooting games!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to slide a target duck clone down by changing its Y coordinate by -15 per tick when it receives a 'duck_hit' broadcast.
questions.task_hint: when I receive 'duck_hit' -> repeat 20 (change 3D position Y by -15) -> delete this clone
questions.explanation: Perfect! This creates a falling gravity death animation, deleting the target when complete!
